title.narrative: Climate Adaptation and Resilience in Thua Thien Hue Province Vietnam (CARe Hue)

description.narrative:
Through the implementation of targeted measures to strengthen the enabling environment and scale up investments in ecosystem-based adaptation, micro-scale infrastructure, and climate-resilient value chains in the agriculture, fisheries and aquaculture sector, the project aims to strengthen the climate-resilience of local communities, and the ecosystems upon which they depend in TT Hue Province. Through targeted support to overcome the aforementioned barriers, ultimately, the project plans to establish TT Hue as a model province for climate change adaptation planning, investing, and monitoring, that can then be replicated in the rest of the country. The project builds on the experiences and lessons learned of LuxDev and the Government of Vietnam, and supports the scaling up of best practices, while establishing an enabling investment environment that will serve as a mechanism to continue to mobilize and channel public and private finance for climate action in the target sectors.
The project will catalyze investments in climate change adaptation, specifically in climate-informed planning and monitoring, ecosystem-based adaptation, micro-scale environmentally friendly infrastructure and disaster risk reduction, through the following outputs (see Theory of Change in annex 3):
* Output 1. Strengthened institutional framework for enhanced climate change adaptation planning, investment, and monitoring * Output 2. Enhanced resilience of ecosystems and the livelihoods of local men and women through EBA interventions and micro-scale environmentally friendly infrastructure * Output 3. Scaling up of climate-resilient practices in the agriculture, fisheries, and aquaculture sector to strengthen the resilience of local ecosystems and the livelihoods that depend on them
Social inclusion and gender-equality are cross-cutting elements throughout the project, as climate change has a disproportionate impact on the livelihoods of women, girls and vulnerable households and communities. As such, the project design will pay close attention to this, and ensure targeted measures are included that acknowledge their differentiated vulnerabilities and needs. The project will be implemented over a 4.5-year period.
OUTPUT 1. STRENGTHENED INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCED CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION PLANNING, INVESTMENT, AND MONITORING
Output 1 focuses on addressing information and capacity constraints for enabling improved responses to climate related hazards in the short-term and facilitate enhanced mid- to long-term climate change adaptation planning, climate change adaptation investments, and monitoring at the commune, district, and provincial levels. Local government agencies will be supported to better prepare for climate-related hazards through: i) enhancing early warning systems and forecasting capacity; ii) facilitating the integration of climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction (DRR) into local climate-informed land use plans; iii) improving their climate change adaptation monitoring and evaluation (M&E) systems; and iv) working with the provincial Forest Protection and Development Fund to develop a mechanism to mobilize additional finance for climate change adaptation. This output is comprised of the following activities and sub-activities:
Activity 1.1: Improving early warning systems and forecasting capacity to allow local government agencies and communities to better prepare for climate-hazards ensuring women are involved in decision making and planning structures
As outlined in Vietnam’s NDC there remains a need for strengthening the capacities of technical staff at local levels to better forecast and prepare for climate related hazards as well as of closing gaps in the provision of climate data and forecasting and warning capacities for extreme weather events. This is evidenced in TT Hue where there is no full-time specialized agency on disaster management at provincial level and within the DONRE Sub-Department of Meteorology and Hydrology and the DARD Sub Department of Irrigation, a limited number of staff are responsible for disaster management on a part-time basis. Thus, human and budgetary resources as well as the necessary equipment are still very limited in order to allow appropriate forecasting for disaster prevention. This activity will support the TT Hue Province in addressing these barriers with the following sub-activities:
Sub-activity 1.1.1: Capacity building of local government authorities through the provision of technical assistance, technology, and equipment
Under this sub-activity support will be provided to local governments to enhance their skills and capacities for forecasting and improving early warning systems. Support will also be provided through the procurement of equipment and advanced technologies for hydrological and meteorological monitoring and forecasting.
Sub-activity 1.1.2: Improving the mechanism of coordination and information sharing amongst national and provincial authorities
This activity will focus on enhancing data flows in the disaster management cycle from national level (VN Disaster Management Authority VNDMA & VN Meteorology and Hydrology Administration VNMHA) to provincial level to systematically implement improved data driven forecasts and risk analysis.
Sub-activity 1.1.3 Improving information dissemination channels and early warnings to local communities to ensure early action
Channels to disseminate information and early warning to local communities will be developed under this sub-activity. Information generated under activity 1.1 will be critical for informing the technical assistance to be provided under output 3 for the farmers and producers in the agriculture, aquaculture, and fisheries sector.
Activity 1.2: Mainstreaming climate adaptation and disaster risk reduction (DRR) into local land use and development planning and investments
This activity will focus on mainstreaming climate adaptation priorities and DRR into local land use and development planning processes to ensure plans are climate-informed and ultimately facilitate investments into climate change adaptation building on lessons learnt and information generated from GCF funded project FP 13. Climate data and information provide a basis for all evidence based DRR activities, including future land use and investment planning. Mainstreaming climate change adaptation in such processes and investments, including in EbA and DRR, requires relevant capacities and data. Therefore, it is crucial to establish respective planning capacities to ensure the systematic use of data and information generated under activity 1.1. The activity supports this through:
Sub-activity 1.2.1: Undertake climate-risk informed local participatory planning processes (LPPP) and Commune Vulnerability Capacity Assessments and integrate climate action into relevant local policies and investment plans.
Under this sub-activity focus will be placed on developing the capacities of local officials to facilitate and undertake climate risk informed LPPP for Socio-Economic Development Planning and DRR at the commune level, considering the differentiated DRR needs of women and men. The information basis for undertaking climate risk informed planning will be developed under activity 1.1. The results of the planning processes will inform activity 1.4 focused on strengthening local financial mechanisms such as the provincial Forest Protection and Development Fund and the selection process for EbA and micro-scale green infrastructure under output 2.
Activity 1.3: Improving climate change adaptation impact monitoring and MRV at the provincial level
To mitigate vulnerability, climate, risks and impacts, tailored systems are needed that generate robust data and ultimately enable policy makers and managers to formulate and plan appropriate climate change response strategies and measures and monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of implemented interventions. This activity will focus on strengthening monitoring for climate change adaptation at the commune, district, and provincial level, ensuring systems are in line with MONRE requirements at the national level. Work under this activity would result in TT Hue becoming the first province in the country with an effectively functioning and reliable M&E system for climate change adaptation that also allows for measuring the climate mitigation impact of cross-cutting interventions. This will increase accountability of both public and private sector actors to implement climate change adaptation measures and will ensure active management to respond to climate change and continuously learn and adapt best practices.
Sub-activity 1.3.1: Support DONRE and DARD in the development of a climate change monitoring system
This sub-activity will focus on providing support to DONRE and DARD in the development of a CCA M&E information system following requirements of the National Climate Change Adaptation Strategy 2021 – 2030, ensuring that data systems are operational, effective, and constantly updated. The climate monitoring system will also allow for measuring the mitigation impact of various cross-cutting interventions, with both mitigation and adaptation impacts.
Activity 1.4: Supporting the provincial Forest Protection and Development Fund for enabling investments in climate resilience in the province
This activity will address the barriers related to lack of financing available for adaptation interventions by assessing the viability to expand the scope and reach of activities that the provincial Forest Protection and Development Fund can fund under its payment for environmental services (PFES) scheme to include payments for active forest-restoration with native species to advance climate change adaptation objectives. It will focus on supporting the FPDF assess and develop a disbursement instrument (e.g. results-based payment) to support the implementation of adaptation interventions including EbA in critically vulnerable areas in the province. In addition, by developing a new disbursement mechanism focused on advancing adaptation objectives from existing financial mechanisms, the project can ensure that financial flows for adaptation interventions will remain in place beyond the implementation of the project.
Sub-activity 1.4.1 Support the fund to design a disbursement mechanism for adaptation investments
Following consultations with FPDF, the fund and provincial authorities will be supported to assess the viability of a new disbursement mechanism for EbA and active forest-restoration investments. In addition, support will be provided for development of eligibility criteria, investment screening, covenants, a monitoring system informed by activity 1.3, and the conditions for its operationalization. As part of the design of the disbursement mechanism, a financial sustainability strategy will be developed to ensure that the disbursement mechanism remains operational over the long-term.
OUTPUT 2. ENHANCED RESILIENCE OF ECOSYSTEMS AND THE LIVELIHOODS OF LOCAL MEN AND WOMEN THROUGH EBA INTERVENTIONS AND MICRO-SCALE ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY INFRASTRUCTURE
To address the climate change risks and impacts on livelihoods of local men and women and the ecosystems on which they depend, as outlined in section B1, this output will support a combination of EbA and micro-scale environmentally friendly infrastructure that will be designed, implemented, managed, and monitored in a participatory manner. The planning under this output will build on the climate-information generated and participatory processes conducted under activity 1.2, and the M&E system developed under activity 1.3 will be used to monitor the impact.
EbA-supported investments under this activity will focus on the restoration of degraded ecosystems and natural and protection forests with site-adapted native tree species to strengthen ecosystems to climate change. Where EbA interventions are not appropriate to address climate risks, the project will support micro-scale environmentally friendly infrastructure. Some EbA and micro-scale infrastructure interventions to be further scoped during the development of the FP are included in annex 08. Specific eligibility criteria will be developed at the outset to ensure that all interventions have minimal or no adverse environmental and/or social risks and impacts (ESS category C).
This output builds on lessons learnt and proof-of-concept established in previous projects in TT Hue and Vietnam and is aligned to the country’s NDC, NAP, and Provincial Climate Change Action Plan 2021-2030. The output is comprised of the following activity and sub-activities:
Activity 2.1: Identification, selection, development, and management of EbA and micro-scale infrastructure
Under this activity information and technical assistance on EbA and micro-scale infrastructure solutions will be provided to local authorities and relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment that facilitates investments in these solutions. Using the information generated under activity 1.2, EbA and micro-scale environmentally friendly infrastructure will be proposed, selected, designed, implemented, and managed in collaboration with local communities to ensure that interventions are meeting specific local needs, are community owned and that investments are sustainable beyond project implementation period.
Sub-activity 2.1.1: Developing an enabling environment to facilitate investments in EbA and environmentally friendly micro-scale infrastructure solutions and technologies
Technical assistance and capacity development on EbA approaches and other environmentally friendly micro-scale infrastructure solutions will be delivered as part of this sub-activity for relevant government authorities (i.e., District/Commune-level line departments of DARD) and community-based organizations and hybrid institutions (i.e. local NGOs / mass organizations such as Women’s Union). This will address existing challenges identified in the NDC of lack of adequate attention being placed on EbA approaches while filling in a knowledge gap about the existence of relatively low-cost micro-scale infrastructure interventions to address climate risks. As part of this sub-activity, eligibility criteria and implementation manual for micro-scale environmentally friendly infrastructure will also be developed to ensure the proposed interventions are fully compliant with ESS risk category C.
Sub-activity 2.1.2: Identification of EbA and environmentally friendly micro-scale infrastructure
Under this activity and based on information generated and participatory planning process conducted under output 1, relevant EbA and micro-scale infrastructure interventions will be identified, ranked, prioritized, and selected based on needs and cost/benefit considerations. The process will be supported by technical advisors who will carry out detailed technical assessments to ensure the adequateness of interventions.[1] As part of this process technical assistance of the communities and community-based organizations will be provided on adequate monitoring and maintenance to interventions during the project implementation period.
Sub-activity 2.1.3: Support district authorities and local communities at commune level with preparation, procurement, implementation, maintenance, and management of selected EbA and micro-scale infrastructure interventions
This sub-activity will focus on supporting district authorities and community-based organizations to prepare, procure necessary material and equipment, and implement or construct prioritized EbA and micro-scale infrastructure interventions and maintain them after project completion. Where EbA interventions are prioritized this can entail the development of community tree nurseries whereas for micro-scale infrastructure it will require the procurement of environmentally friendly technologies and materials (for instance, elastocoast).
OUTPUT 3. SCALING UP OF CLIMATE-RESILIENT FISHERIES AND AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES TO STRENGTHEN THE RESILIENCE OF LOCAL ECOSYSTEMS AND THE LIVELIHOODS THAT DEPEND ON THEM
As outlined in section B.1, climate change is already having an impact on agriculture, aquaculture, and fisheries’ production and productivity in TT Hue and current strategies to maintain productivity despite the impacts from climate change, such as the indiscriminate use of chemical fertilizer, are giving rise to food safety issues and further deterioration of ecosystems that in turn increases vulnerabilities to climate change. There is, thus, a need for adapting and diversifying agricultural, fisheries, and aquaculture practices to increase productivity, incomes, and resilience to threats posed by climate change. Output 3 is complementary to output 2, while activities under output 2 focus on protecting men and women in TT Hue against climate change hazards, activities under output 3 focus on supporting the diversification and enhanced resilience of livelihoods through the promotion of climate resilient productive practices. Communes targeted under investments in output 2 will also be supported with investments under output 3 to ensure that synergies across outputs are realized.
Specifically, the activities under output 3 will support farmers to implement and scale climate-resilient investments for key local value chains and strengthen their management and technical capacities to develop short- and medium-term climate-informed adaptation plans and strategies; providing climate-sensitive technical assistance; supporting the adoption of climate resilient models. In addition, it will support value chain development and market access for products produced via climate resilient practices. To help overcome barriers for financing climate-resilient agricultural practices and value chains, the project will work with financial intermediaries such as Agribank and the Women’s Union Fund to develop or tailor existing financial products to the specific characteristics of climate-resilient models (e.g., considering suitable amounts, tenor, alternative sources of collateral, repayment schedules, among others).
Activity 3.1: Implement and scale up climate-resilient agriculture, aquaculture, and fisheries models and practices for key local value chains
This activity will support the introduction of production technologies and practices in agriculture and aquaculture that enhance the resilience to climate impacts and maximize food security while also addressing concerns around food safety in the province. Models will be scoped and selected in collaboration with CIAT experts during the development of the FP. Potential models to be considered include: climate-resilient practices for rice such as System of Rice Intensification (SRI), Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) and rice–shrimp or rice–fish diversified systems key increasing resilience to drought, floods, pest and diseases while also delivering mitigation co-benefits[2]; water-saving irrigation practices such as drip or sprinkler irrigation and moisture preservation[3]; adoption of improved (non-GMO nor invasive) crop varieties resistant to droughts, flood, salinity, or pests and diseases e.g. in rice, maize, fruits, legumes[4]; high yielding varieties resistant to major climatic risks and requiring minimum chemical inputs; intercropping systems with annual crops (e.g. corn, legumes) and agroforestry models integrating fruits and indigenous trees in mountainous areas (for income diversification, improved productivity, reduced soil erosion/moisture loss, improved soil fertility)[5]; edible insect farming as income generating activity or low-cost nutrition supplement[6], and poly-aquaculture and shrimp production integrated with shrimp-forest farming in mangroves e.g. to deal with saltwater intrusion[7]. The activity will benefit from the experiences and lessons learned generated during the piloting of organic agriculture models by LuxDev[8] and current efforts to establish an organic agriculture association and develop an industry in TT Hue.
Sub-activity 3.1.1: Strengthen farmer management and technical capacities in support of resilient and sustainable livelihoods
This sub-activity will focus on strengthening the knowledge, management, and technical capacities of farmers and farmer associations for enhancing climate change adaptation planning and enabling the adoption of climate-resilient production models and sound post-harvest practices. This sub-activity will also include the provision of technical assistance on financial management capacities, business and marketing plan development that can facilitate the development of bankable projects that can be financed by local financial intermediaries or private investors. It will also include targeted support for women-owned and women-led climate-resilient businesses in the target sectors.
Sub-activity 3.1.2: Provision of climate-informed technical assistance to support adoption of climate-resilient production models
Under this sub-activity, climate-informed technical assistance will be provided to farmers. This will entail refining and co-designing risk mitigation strategies and implementation plans with local stakeholders based on: (i) high resolution risk assessment (hazard and crop suitability modelling, soil analysis); (ii) the definition of targeted priorities for climate-resilient models for climate risk mitigation in agriculture and aquaculture for specific coastal, lagoon, low-lying and upland localities; and (iii) development of robust systems to monitor implementation. Plans under this sub-activity will be informed by climate data generated under output 1.
Sub-activity 3.1.3: Market access and development of climate-resilient value chains
This sub-activity will focus on improving market access for climate-resilient agriculture, aquaculture, and fisheries products to maximize the benefits to farmers from the adoption of improved technologies and practices. It will build on the linkages amongst farmers, cooperatives, and private companies developed under an existing LuxDev pilot focused on organic agriculture (a potential growth industry as identified by TT Hue authorities), as well as focus on strengthening participatory guarantee systems (PGS) to facilitate consumer trust in a manner that is accessible to small farmers.
Activity 3.2: Development of tailored financial products and services for climate-resilient agriculture, aquaculture, and fisheries
Access to finance remains an important barrier for the adoption of climate-resilient agriculture and aquaculture practices.[9] Under this activity, work will be carried out with local financial institutions (LFIs) to enable a better understanding of gender-responsive climate-resilient models and of their risks, with the aim to develop approaches for LFIs to finance these investments. This would involve also ensuring LFIs are capable of screening and monitoring these investments. While the specific activities will focus first on working with LFIs with a mandate for working with the prioritized sectors – such as Agribank and the Women’s Union Funds – all knowledge and products generated, and emerging lessons will be shared within the industry and to other relevant stakeholders to ensure that financing models can be applied by other actors in TT Hue and the rest of the country. Sub-activities include:
Sub-activity 3.2.1: Support and promote the development of tailored financial products for climate-resilient agriculture and aquaculture
Under this sub-activity technical assistance will be provided to LFIs with initial focus on Agribank and the Women’s Union Fund on gender-responsive climate-resilient agriculture and aquaculture models, the risks associated with those models and on the characteristics of potential products to finance them. For this sub-activity, the project aims to leverage the experience and expertise of Agribank financing organic agriculture, its experience with green lending programmes, as well as the enabling framework established by the State Bank of Vietnam in the Action plan of the banking sector for implementation of the National Strategy for Green Growth 2020 to develop products with preferential conditions for climate-resilient investments that can be scaled outside of the province. During the development of this concept note, consultations were held with Agribank that expressed willingness in collaborating in identifying mechanisms for financing climate-resilient investments in agriculture, aquaculture, and fisheries in the province, and it was agreed that a letter of intent will be prepared for outlining collaboration during the preparation of the funding proposal. The project will also work with the Women’s Union fund, a fund initially capitalized by LuxDev to support the development of tailored financial products for climate-resilient investments.
Sub-activity 3.2.2: Support for LFIs for environmental and social (E&S) screening and climate impact monitoring monitor the climate impacts of their investments
As part of this sub-activity technical assistance will be provided to LFIs to screen the E&S impacts of potential investments in climate-resilient production projects through, amongst others, the development of eligibility criteria and systematic E&S risk analysis, and to develop a system that allows them to monitor the climate impacts of their investments.
Sub-activity 3.2.3 – Raising awareness of organizations, cooperatives, and associations on financing opportunities, including women’s organizations
This sub-activity will develop and execute plans to raise awareness about existing financing opportunities identified under sub-activity 3.2.1 amongst farmers, associations, and cooperatives to ensure that financial products are utilized. Women and women’s organizations will be also targeted by this activity to ensure they are in a capacity to access finance from either LFIs or the Women’s Union fund.
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
LuxDev will act as the Accredited Entity (AE) and Executing Entity (EE) of this GCF SAP project. In its role as AE, LuxDev will coordinate with the GCF Secretariat, select and recruit a professional team of technical advisors (TA) to work within TT Hue’s DPI a critical project partner, in close collaboration and cooperation with a select team of existing DPI staff, and ensure general oversight and management of project implementation in line with GCF standards and requirements. These tasks will be the responsibility of LuxDev’s headquarters in Luxembourg and the relevant business units, with direct support and guidance from the Environment and Climate Change Expert (who is also the GCF focal point), the Sustainable and Innovative Finance Expert, and a Programme Adviser, and with additional support of the LuxDev Regional Office staff based in Vientiane/Lao PDR. In its role as EE, and through a professional team of advisers and support staff led by a chief technical adviser based in Hué/Vietnam, LuxDev will assess the capacity of, and engage the relevant public and private entities based on their ability to use GCF proceeds and/or implement the GCF funded activities in accordance with GCF policies and requirements, coordinate with relevant partners and all project stakeholders, set up all necessary operational arrangements, and ensure smooth implementation of the project’s planned technical components and activities, in line with project objectives and expected results. The AE will collaborate with the following partners: the International Center for Tropical Agriculture (CIAT), with office in Hanoi, has an MOU signed with the AE and will support the TA team in Hue with activities in climate resilient agriculture. And Hue University and several private local research outfits that have supported earlier Luxembourg CCA interventions in various ways, will be available for similar support to a GCF funded intervention. Further, collaboration agreements with the Women’s Union, Agribank, the provincial Forest Protection and Development Fund will be formalized during the inception phase of the project, defining roles and responsibilities.

PRELIMINARY IDENTIFICATION OF RISKS
Preliminary technical and operational risks have been identified during the development of the concept note. Preliminary risks identified at this stage are as follows: changes in political circumstances result in support on project from national, provincial, and local governments not being sustained throughout project implementation; proposed or implemented EbA and micro-scale infrastructure interventions identified from participatory process are not relevant or adequate to address most relevant climate-related hazards; limited willingness of local men and women to participate in the implementation and monitoring of EbA and micro-scale projects; limited willingness of small producers in the agricultural, aquaculture, and fisheries sector to adopt climate-resilient practices; and continued potential impacts arising from prolonged COVID19. These risks and their associated mitigation strategies will be fully scoped during the development of the pre-feasibility study and funding proposal.
MONITORING AND EVALUATION
A Results Based Monitoring Framework (RBMF) will be established to monitor progress and to capture intermediate and outcome results. The RBMF is built on M&E systems designed by LuxDev for earlier climate change adaptation interventions in Vietnam, considered a best practice for Monitoring for Results by the final evaluation team of one of the interventions (VIE/033), and subsequently adopted by LuxDev as a corporate model. Based on that RBMF data system, the project can produce clear results-based progress reports. In addition, an independent mid-term evaluation as well as an independent final evaluation will be conducted according to the conditions specified in the funded activity agreement (FAA).
